title: SUPPORTING AND LIMITING FACTORS IN INCLUSIVE EDUCATION IN PRE-PRIMARY AND PRIMARY SCHOOLS: AN OVERVIEW OF EMPIRICAL FINDINGS IN THE SLOVAK CONTEXT
abstract: Inclusive education in pre-primary and primary schools depends on the interplay of several interconnected factors at the levels of the teacher, the school, and the broader support system. This paper is a review study aimed at identifying and analysing the factors that support and limit inclusive education, with a focus on the Slovak context. A search for empirical studies was conducted in the Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar databases. Based on predefined criteria, 14 empirical studies were included in the final analysis. The findings were organised into three thematic areas: factors at the teacher level, factors at the school level and school-based support, and the Slovak context as an interpretative framework for the implementation of inclusive education. The analysis showed that inclusive practice are supported by positive teacher attitudes, practical experience, professional preparedness, collaboration with specialist staff, and the functioning of school support mechanisms. The main limiting factors included insufficient professional preparation, uncertainty in differentiated instruction, a lack of specialist staff, administrative burden, and broader systemic barriers

title: NURTURING THE DEVELOPMENT OF CHILDREN WITH AUTISM SPECTRUM DISORDERS THROUGH LEISURE ACTIVITIES
abstract: The paper underscores the crucial role of leisure activities in the development of children with autism spectrum disorders. It aims to provide a theoretical basis for understanding autism spectrum disorders and the significance of leisure time in their development. The paper also proposes practical recommendations on how to effectively use leisure time to support children with autism spectrum disorders. The research effort was based on the synthesis of professional literature, data obtained through a questionnaire survey, and interviews with experts and parents, thus providing a comprehensive overview of the current opportunities and challenges faced by children with autism spectrum disorders in leisure activities

title: EDUCATION OF CONVICTED PERSONS IN SLOVAK AND CZECH SCHOLARLY LITERATURE
abstract: The paper addresses the issue of the education of convicted persons. The aim of the paper is to present, through a review study, selected Slovak and Czech authors who focus on adult education in the specific environment of imprisonment and the subsequent reintegration into society. Attention is given to the analysis of their professional focus and approaches in selected publications that reflect the current state of knowledge in this field. The paper highlights the fact that, in the Slovak context, the issue of the education of convicted persons has been developed to a lesser extent and is mainly represented by authors oriented towards andragogy and social pedagogy. In contrast, in the Czech context, a broader range of authors can be identified who approach this issue also from the perspectives of penology, criminology, and the systemic functioning of the prison system. The result of the paper is a synthesis of knowledge from selected authors and an emphasis on the importance of educating convicted persons as a tool for resocialization and the prevention of recidivism. At the same time, differences between Slovak and Czech approaches to this issue are identified, and possibilities

title: RESEARCH METHODS USED IN STUDIES OF EFL PRONUNCIATION INSTRUCTION: A MAPPING REVIEW
abstract: This mapping review explores the research methods used in recent studies (2020–2025) on EFL pronunciation instruction. Following PRISMA guidelines, peer-reviewed, open-access studies were identified through Web of Science, Scopus, and ERIC. Nine studies were analysed in terms of research approach, research design, and data collection and data analysis methods. The findings reveal a strong dominance of quantitative and mixed-methods approaches, especially pre-test–post-test designs and inferential statistical analysis, while qualitative approaches remain underrepresented in current research.

title: ANALYSIS OF MATHEMATICS PROBLEMS IN EXTERNAL EXAMS FROM THE PERSPECTIVE OF VISUAL IMPAIRMENT
abstract: This paper analyzes external assessment tasks from a special education perspective. The aim is to identify informational and visual barriers that affect the accessibility, comprehensibility, and solvability of math problems for this group of students. The analysis evaluates both the content and form of the math problems, particularly their visual presentation, linguistic formulation, use of graphic elements, and possibilities for tactile or auditory adaptation. The paper highlights the need for adaptation and appropriate modifications in the areas of formatting, individualization, and alternative forms of presenting mathematical tasks that respect the individual needs of students with visual impairments. Based on these findings, recommendations are formulated for the creation of accessible math problems that enable the objective and fair assessment of the mathematical knowledge and competencies of students with visual impairments.

title: CURRENT CHALLENGES IN IMPLEMENTING CONTEMPORARY CHAMBER MUSIC IN MUSIC EDUCATION AT ELEMENTARY ART SCHOOLS
abstract: This paper examines the current challenges of integrating contemporary chamber music into the educational process at elementary arts schools. It takes the form of a theoretical-analytical and narrative-overview study based on professional literature, curricular documents, and institutional contexts. Chamber music is understood as a specific domain of music education in which the interpretive, perceptual, communicative, cooperative, and reflective dimensions of learning are intertwined. The study identifies five interrelated levels of implementation: methodological-didactic, personnel, curricular, repertoire, and institutional. At the same time, it creates a conceptual framework for further research and opens a discussion on the possibilities for content and methodological innovation in music education at elementary art schools.

title: PROGRAMME ESKI AND EXECUTIVE FUNCTION TRAINING IN STUDENTS WITH DEVELOPMENTAL LEARNING DISABILITIES
abstract: The study provides a brief theoretical overview of executive functions in the context of pupils with specific learning disabilities and empirically examines the effectiveness of the ESKI training programme. The programme was developed due to the limited availability of comprehensive intervention programmes in the Slovak context. Its content includes the areas of planning, organization, working memory, flexibility, self-monitoring, and self-control. The main aim of the study was to verify the effectiveness of the ESKI training programme at the level of the overall executive function score in pupils with specific learning disabilities. The research sample consisted of eight pupils from two primary schools in the districts of Zvolen and Nitra. The level of executive functions was assessed using the DEF questionnaire by Dawson and Guare (2012) and an author-designed self-assessment questionnaire of executive functions. The results showed a statistically significant improvement in the overall score after completing the training programme in both research instruments. The findings suggest that the ESKI training programme may represent a practically applicable special-pedagogical interven

title: THE PEDAGOGICAL LEGACY OF JÁN SEBERÍNI IN THE CONTEXT OF TODAY'S EDUCATION
abstract: The study deals with the pedagogic and social contribution of Ján Michal Seberíni (1780–1857), an evangelical clergyman, pedagogue and educational reformer, whose significance goes beyond the boundaries of his time and reaches into contemporary pedagogical theory and practice. The article presents his life destinies, the main pedagogical principles contained in his work On the main principles of initial education for educators and their duties (1810) and analyzes their connection with current pedagogical concepts. The author of the emphasizes Seberín's emphasis on the mother tongue, individualization in teaching, all-round development of the child's personality and the teacher's ethical responsibility, thereby anticipating modern pedagogical paradigms such as constructivism or inclusive pedagogy.

title: SELF-EFFICACY AND COLLECTIVE EFFICACY AS PREDICTORS OF ASSISTANT BYSTANDER BEHAVIOR IN BULLYING SITUATIONS
abstract: Bullying is a serious social phenomenon that negatively affects the psychological development of children and adolescents. Despite growing interest in the issue of bystanders in bullying, the question of the factors that influence assisting behavior toward the aggressor remains under-researched. The aim of this study is to analyze the role of self-efficacy and group efficacy in the context of assiting behavior toward the bully in bullying among elementary school students. The research sample consisted of 377 elementary school students (M=13.45, SD=4.02). The research battery consisted of the following instruments: Scale of Bystander Behavior in Bullying (Thornberg et al., 2017), General Self-Efficacy Scale (Schwarzer, Jerusalem, 1995), Collective Efficacy Scale (Barchia &Bussey, 2011a,b) , and the Student Bullying/Victimization Questionnaire (Olweus, 1996). Self-efficacy was negatively correlated with assisting behavior toward the bully. Self-efficacy and collective efficacy emerged as significant predictors of assisting behavior toward the bully. The results highlight the need for intervention programs that simultaneously develop students’ individual self-efficacy and the group co

title: PARENTING STYLES AS DETERMINANTS OF ADOLESCENT RISK BEHAVIOR
abstract: Presented study examines the relationship between parenting styles and adolescents’ propensity toward risk behavior. The primary aim was to analyze how different parenting approaches are associated with the occurrence of various forms of adolescent risk behavior. A quantitative research design was employed using a survey method, incorporating two standardized instruments: the Risk Behavior Inventory (RSI) and the Parental Parenting Style Questionnaire. The research sample consisted of 132 secondary school students aged 16–19 years from southern Slovakia. Data were analyzed using non-parametric tests and Spearman’s correlation analysis. The findings revealed statistically significant gender differences in selected domains of risk behavior, with boys reporting higher levels of externalizing behaviors, particularly bullying and delinquency, online risk behavior, and substance use. In contrast, girls showed slightly higher levels of problematic eating habits, although these differences were not consistently statistically significant. Regarding parenting styles, the results indicated that authoritarian and neglectful parenting were positively associated with higher levels of adolescent

title: FROM 3D SCANNERS TO SMARTPHONE-BASED DIGITAL ANTHROPOMETRY: A PRELIMINARY METHODOLOGICAL STUDY FOR PHYSICAL EDUCATION AND SPORTS PEDAGOGY
abstract: The study presents the SOMATON digital anthropometry framework and preliminary results from 363 anonymized 3D body scans. It examines whether smartphone-based image data could become a scalable complement to 3D scanning for estimating body dimensions, joint positions and morphological typology in physical education and sports pedagogy.

title: TEACHERS' OPINIONS ON THE ROLE AND PLACEMENT OF DEFENCE EDUCATION IN CONTEMPORARY SCHOOL
abstract: The study aimed to examine teachers' views on the implementation of defence education in contemporary Slovak schools. The research method was an online interview conducted on a sample of Slovak teachers selected from two primary and two secondary schools. The results showed that defence education is not sufficiently included in the schools, most teachers have a positive attitude towards its importance and assess the preparedness of pupils as insufficient. Teachers state that pupils' reactions to the current implementation of exercises in schools vary from highly positive, ambiguous to the smaller proportion of negative. Teachers do not have specific training in these topics, nor do they know what opportunities exist for further training. Cooperation with other experts is limited. Findings suggest that research and implementation of modern content and teacher training are important because of the need for measures in the interest of national security.

title: APPRECIATING THE SOCIAL AND EMOTIONAL ASPECTS OF TEACHING
abstract: We believe that for this paper, the ideas of the world-famous authors C. Rogers: "We are educated, but evil" and E. Fromm: "We are in the twenty-first century with our minds, but our hearts are in the Stone Age". However, we will immediately point out and emphasise that these ideas are, unfortunately, worldwide and do not apply to this or that country. A sketch of why this is so is also offered in this post. In line with the above quote, this article deals with the social and emotional aspects of education. This is an area that deserves special attention from all parents and teachers.

title: WELL-BEING, TEST ANXIETY AND LANGUAGE PERFORMANCE IN THE CONTEXT OF LANGUAGE TESTING
abstract: This article focuses on the relationship between well-being, test anxiety, and language performance in the context of language testing. The aim is to synthesize current research on the interplay between emotional and psychological factors and testing conditions, and their impact on performance in language examinations. The review shows that test anxiety represents a significant negative factor, the effects of which are shaped by contextual and individual determinants. It further highlights the need for comprehensive and integrated approaches to supporting well-being in language education.

title: WE NEED MORE WELLBEING, POSITIVE MOTIVATION AND RESILIENCE IN SCHOOLS
abstract: The importance of a good emotional environment, which is important and influential for pupils' learning, has been increasingly emphasised recently, including in the context of the forthcoming education reform. These requirements are well known to teachers and many apply them in their pedagogical and didactic activities. Emotionality has a particularly significant impact on well-being in the classroom, which is also supported by positive teaching. The paper describes several aspects related to wellbeing and also to the concept of progressive teaching. However, the reality of education is that wellbeing needs more attention. This aspect is also highlighted by the results of international measures of educational achievement and pupils' lives in schools. In this paper, we emphasize positive education and resilience, which have a significant impact on the quality of wellbeing.

title: FOUNDATIONS AND FUTURE DIRECTIONS IN PRONUNCIATION TEACHING: A LITERATURE REVIEW
abstract: The English language is known for very complex pronunciation, influencing the overall communicative competence and all four language skills. Perhaps due to the fear of this complexity, teaching pronunciation is often considered daunting and relegated to the background of teaching priorities. This literature review investigates the historical background of pronunciation instruction, updated methodological approaches, and current trends in the area. New studies deal mainly with the use of digital technologies and computer- and mobile-assisted training, Attention is also given to the rising use of artificial intelligence and augmented reality in pronunciation teaching. By linking the theoretical foundations with the empirical findings of this review, the need for continuous efforts for innovation and quality teacher training in the field of pronunciation teaching arises. It is also possible to identify a research gap in the insufficient application of neuroscience findings to pronunciation teaching practice, which calls for future research in this matter.

title: PEDAGOGY OF FORESTRY
abstract: The authors of the article focus on forestry pedagogy and its specifics from its beginnings at the first forestry school to the present, while attention will also be paid to the arboretum itself and its mission and use in education. The work is devoted to the historical development of the Hrádok Arboretum, as an exceptional object of the Forestry and Timber School in Liptovský Hrádek. Let us present the most important milestones in its development, its important position in the education of pupils. We focus on the pedagogy of forestry and its specifics in the past, connecting the information gathered in the chapters devoted to the history of education. We point out the educational contribution of the arboretum. And not only within professional forestry subjects or natural science subjects. It also serves as a space for teaching local history, which is hidden in its inanimate and living parts.

title: https://www.pegasjournal.eu/2025_14_01_06.html
abstract: The aim of the study was to develop the Didactic Analysis and Evaluation of Method Books (DAEM) evaluation tool for the systematic evaluation of method books. The tool analyses three apparatuses (presentation of the curriculum, the control of curriculum acquisition, orientation) and three categories of components (verbal, notational, pictorial). The DAEM was applied to a sample of 12 method books. The highest quality was achieved by the guitar and recorder textbooks, while the accordion method books lagged. The results provide a practical framework for evaluating method books and can contribute to their improvement in music pedagogy.

title: THE DEVELOPMENT OF THE SLOVAK DEAF COMMUNITY DURING THE 20TH CENTURY
abstract: The paper deals with the history of care and education of people who are deaf and hard of hearing and the development of the Slovak Deaf Community in the 20th century. It presents the existence of institutes and schools for deaf pupils and later for pupils with hearing impairment in Slovakia, as well as civic associations of the deaf. It explains the views on the use of sign language in the teaching. The paper introduces job opportunities and sports activities for people who are deaf or hard of hearing, as well as the accessibility of mass media.

title: QUALITY OF FURTHER EDUCATION COURSES FOR PEDAGOGICAL STAFF IN THE FIELD OF ART EDUCATION IN THE CZECH REPUBLIC
abstract: The contribution presents partial results of a study dealing with the quality of further education programs for teaching staff of primary and secondary schools in the field of art education in the Czech Republic. The presented data, obtained through a questionnaire survey conducted among selected institutions providing further education courses for teaching staff in this field, provides information on the ways in which institutions set the quality parameters of their courses and monitor their level. Attention is also paid to the evaluation of the quality of the lecturers of the educational courses and to possible ways of improving their quality. The sub-results should contribute to the understanding of the current state of continuing education courses for art educators in terms of quality and help to set the way forward for research aimed at improving the quality of these courses.

title: INTERPRETATION OF CONTEMPORARY CHAMBER MUSIC BY SLOVAK COMPOSERS AT PRIMARY ART SCHOOLS: CHALLENGES, PRACTICE AND PERSPECTIVES
abstract: This study deals with the interpretation of chamber compositions by contemporary Slovak composers in the environment of primary art schools (ZUŠ). The aim is to analyze the availability of suitable musical literature, the level of interest on the part of teachers and pupils and the possibilities of methodological incorporation of these works into teaching. Based on a questionnaire survey among teachers and pupils, it identifies barriers and potentials of working with contemporary repertoire and formulates recommendations for practice.

title: DYNAMIC ASSESSMENT OF PRESCHOOL CHILDREN: METHODOLOGICAL IMPLICATIONS OF THE ACFS METHOD
abstract: This paper deals with the issue of dynamic diagnosis of cognitive and executive functions in preschool children, focusing on the use of the ACFS method as a tool for assessing a child's potential and current performance. The aim of the study is to describe, analyze, and apply the selected ACFS method in preschool children. In addition to the theoretical framework, the study also includes the conclusions of empirical research obtained through a qualitative research design, created by a methodological context consisting of a combination of the application of the ACFS method of dynamic assessment, observation, and anamnestic questionnaires, which were then compiled into detailed case studies. The research sample consisted of two carefully selected cases where the application of the ACFS method revealed significant differences between pre-test and post-test performance, especially in areas with identified deficits. The changes recorded point to the importance of the interventions that dynamic assessment enables and demonstrate the method's ability to support adaptive cognitive development, flexibility of thinking, and the acquisition of effective learning strategies. These findings doc

title: EMOTION AI IN EDUCATION: EXPLORING THE RESEARCH POTENTIAL OF MORPHCAST
abstract: Nowadays, modern technologies and artificial intelligence play an increasingly important role not only in the educational process but also in academic research. One of the innovative tools in this area is the MorphCast AI-powered software tool, which uses Emotion AI technology – a form of artificial intelligence capable of analyzing and interpreting emotional reactions based on non-verbal expressions, such as facial expressions. The paper aims to present the possibilities of using MorphCast within research projects. It describes the main functions of the software, its advantages in capturing affective reactions, as well as methodological and ethical issues associated with its use. The paper aims to discuss the potential of artificial intelligence-based technologies in developing innovative educational approaches.

title: ASSESSING CRITICAL THINKING INTERVENTIONS IN UNIVERSITY STUDENTS: A LITERATURE REVIEW OF INSTRUMENTS
abstract: The development of critical thinking (CT) is essential for students to participate effectively in a modern society. Still, studies show a lack of clarity of concepts, used methods and measures of intervention. This review focuses on measurement instruments used in critical thinking interventions, evaluating their psychometric properties. A literature search was conducted in three scientific databases - Scopus, Web Of Science, PubMed. The data were systematically retrieved in two phases by two independent researchers following the PRISMA flow diagram. Overall, 13 studies were included in the final analysis. The most frequently used instruments were the California Critical Thinking Skills Test (CCTST) (Facione, 1990) for assessing skills and the California Critical Thinking Disposition Inventory (CTDI) for dispositions. The review also identified a concerning trend of poor psychometric reporting across studies.

title: PHONICS APPROACH IN THE UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
abstract: The article concentrates on the historical evolution of the Phonics approach in the United States of America. The objective of the paper is to evaluate and elucidate the primary distinctions between Systematic and Non-Systematic Phonics through a comparative analysis. The qualitative approach delineates clear differences and facilitates an understanding of the methodology of English language instruction within a native context. The findings are advantageous for educators and linguists engaged in English literacy development.

title: FUTURE TEACHERS AND THE DIGITAL AGE, APPROVAL OF THE TEACHER EDUCATION PROGRAM AND STUDENTS' DIGITAL LITERACY LEVELS
abstract: The study aims to analyze the relationship between the study program and the level of digital competences of students in teacher education programs. Five categories of digital competence in student teacher education programs were analyzed to determine the extent to which the focus of the teacher education program, the approbation, can be significant in terms of the quality of individuals' digital competences. The theoretical framework is based on current concepts of digital literacy, European standards of digital competences and pedagogical readiness for technology-supported teaching.

title: MORNING CIRCLES AS A TOOL OF INCLUSIVE EDUCATION AND UNIVERSAL PREVENTION: A COMPARATIVE ANALYSIS OF CLASS TEACHERS’ PERCEPTIONS AND THEIR SUBJECTIVE WELL-BEING
abstract: This study focuses on morning circles as a part of pedagogical practice at the primary level of education in the context of inclusive education and universal prevention. The main aim of the research was to identify differences in the core attributes of implementing morning circles among class teachers. The research also explored the subjective experience of teachers’ habitual emotional well-being during morning circles, as well as the differentiated perception of behavioral manifestations in boys and girls participating in these activities. The research design was a comparative quantitative study. Three instruments were used for data collection: the Subjective Emotional Habitual Well-being Scale (SEHP) (Dzuka, Dalbert, 2002), the shortened Conners' Questionnaire for Teachers and Parents (Paclt, Sebek, 1998; in: Paclt et al., 2007), and an author-designed, non-standardized questionnaire. The results showed that 75.00% of participants disagreed with the exclusive implementation of morning circles by class teachers. The average score for positive emotional experience during morning circles reached a value of M = 3.5, while negative experience was less frequent (M = 2.08). In assessing

title: FUTURE TEACHERS’ ATTITUDES TOWARD INCLUSION: EMPIRICAL FINDINGS FROM 2020 AND 2025
abstract: The paper analyses the attitudes of future teachers towards inclusive education in the context of educational reforms supported by the Slovak Recovery and Resilience Plan. It aims to identify which attitude components—cognitive, affective, and behavioral—have changed significantly between 2020 and 2025. The research uses the standardized MATIES scale, whose Slovak version proved to be valid and reliable. The results indicate the most positive shift in the affective component (emotional readiness for diversity), while the cognitive component (belief in the universal right to inclusion) remains weaker. The paper concludes with recommendations for teacher training and public policy.

title: EDUCATIONAL COMIC AS A TOOL FOR INCLUSIVE EDUCATION
abstract: The paper explores the potential of educational comics as a tool for inclusive education. Thanks to their multimodal nature and visual-narrative structure, comics can support understanding and motivation among students with different mother tongues and specific learning disorders. The study reflects on theoretical concepts of inclusion, the characteristics of educational comics, their advantages and limitations, and includes examples from teaching practice.

title: EXPLORING TEACHERS' EXPECTATIONS OF DISCIPLINARY LITERACIES: AN ANALYSIS OF INSIGHTS FROM ALBANIA
abstract: This research aims to examine the expectations of Albanian educators regarding disciplinary literacies, emphasizing the specific skills necessary for successful participation in various academic fields, including reading, writing, and communication. The main research question investigates: How do Albanian teachers perceive disciplinary literacy, and in what ways do these perceptions affect their teaching methods? Employing a qualitative research approach, data were gathered via detailed individual interviews with educators and observations of the classroom. The main findings indicate that educators view disciplinary literacy as essential for students' educational achievement and future goals, highlighting the importance of vocabulary relevant to the discipline, critical thinking skills, and effective communication. Challenges noted include insufficient instructional time, oversized class sizes, restricted access to resources, and professional development focused on disciplinary literacy. Educators often utilize direct teaching of subject-specific vocabulary and group learning exercises to fill these gaps. Suggestions include incorporating disciplinary literacy goals into curriculum

title: SELF-EFFICACY OF BEGINNING TEACHERS IN THE FIELD OF PEDAGOGICAL DIAGNOSTICS OF THE FAMILY ENVIRONMENT
abstract: The author of the study addresses the issue of pedagogical diagnostics of the family environment. The qualitative research aimed to identify key factors that determine the level of assessment of beginning teachers’ self-efficacy in the field of pedagogical diagnostics of the family. The research sample consisted of 17 Slovak beginning teachers (novices, with a maximum of five years of pedagogical experience), with whom two focus groups were conducted. The obtained results pointed to the main determinants of teachers’ self-assessment (self-confidence) in the given area. The decisive factor turned out to be mainly the amount of practical experience with parents. The research confirmed that the extent of this experience significantly influences the perception of one's own competence. Moreover, we found that teachers who had the opportunity to work more closely with a motivated induction teacher evaluate their diagnostic competences in relation to the pupil’s family environment somewhat more positively. Beginning teachers are also able to identify key areas in which their diagnostic competencies related to the pupil’s family environment need to be further developed. The research result

title: MOVEMENT-BASED INTERVENTION IN PRE-SCHOOL EDUCATION: AN EMPIRICAL STUDY ON THE DEVELOPMENT OF BASIC MOTOR SKILLS
abstract: It is important to stimulate the proper motor development of children from an early age. The pre-school period represents a highly sensitive stage during which fundamental movement skills are developed. Various movement programs are used to support this development. The aim of our study was to verify the effectiveness of a program designed by us, focused on fundamental athletic skills, in improving selected motor abilities of pre-school children. The research involved 24 children aged 5–6 years. Selected tests from the Deutscher Motorik Test (DMT) and MOBAK test batteries were used. Testing was conducted before the application of the intervention program and after six weeks of regular exercise. A positive effect of the proposed six-week athletic movement program for children aged 5–6 years implemented in a kindergarten setting was demonstrated in the tests of 10-meter sprint, standing long jump, deep forward bend, and throwing accuracy.

title: INTERDISCIPLINARY OVERLAPS OF TECHNICS AND ART IN EDUCATIONAL PROCESS
abstract: The article deals with the possibilities and benefits of interdisciplinary connections of technics and art in the educational process of primary schools. The aim is to point out the common intersections of both subject areas, which can be effectively used to develop creativity, technical thinking, aesthetic feeling and practical skills of students. The text analyzes the connections of content standards in the curriculum of technical and art education in primary school at the 2nd level of education. The article offers the specific didactic approaches that enable integrated teaching, as well as specific examples of creative activities combining technical and art elements. The conclusion of the article brings examples and recommendations for educators on how to effectively plan and implement teaching with an emphasis on the mutual connection of technical and art aspects.

title: FUTURE CLASSROOM LAB: AN INNOVATIVE APPROACH TO DIGITAL INCLUSION AND THE DEVELOPMENT OF DIGITAL COMPETENCIES IN EDUCATION
abstract: This article explores the possibilities for implementing and utilizing a 21st-century classroom concept designed for kindergartens and primary schools. The aim is to present both the theoretical foundations and practical aspects of implementing the Future Classroom Laboratory (FCL), with a focus on interdisciplinary connections, support for inclusive education, modernization of digital infrastructure, and the integration of modular furniture into existing school environments. We analyze the opportunities and challenges associated with the transition to digital learning environments and discuss the evolving role of the teacher as a qualified professional in the digital age.

title: UNIVERSITY LANGUAGE PROGRAMS: THE EARLY SIGNS OF UNDERLYING PROFESSIONALIZATION
abstract: This article analyzes the integration of professional skills into language university programs, with a particular focus on the French language degree. It highlights an interactive dynamic between theoretical knowledge and practical skills, emphasizing how these elements complement each other to prepare students for the demands of the job market while maintaining a balance with academic values. The article proposes curricular adjustments to reinforce this dynamic and integrate 21st-century skills, while also suggesting research perspectives to evaluate the impact of these reforms on graduates' employability.

title: ADAPTATION OF PIANO PIECE OF BELA KELER – ROMANTIC LIFE OP. 101 TO BE USED IN PIANO PEDAGOGIC
abstract: Piano piece Romantic life op. 101 celebrates its 180th anniversary this year. Originally the piece was named Waltz of Bardejov Spa season 1844, referring to the birth place of the author. Bela Keler was one of the most important composer of salon music of 19th century. Kelers work represent cultural heritage, we would like to introduce to the wider audience. Based on todays requirements, it requires certain modifications mostly due to the interpretation. Romantic life op. 101 is extensive piano piece refering to the Bardejov spa. It represents ideal oportunity for adaptations to the easier piano arrangement. We created the arangements of this waltz that are for piano student of the Elementary music schools with various technical levels starting from easiest to the more difficult ones. Thanks to these arrangements, students in the first year of piano playing, will have the opportunity to actively familiarize themselves with the work of our important composer who comes from the territory of todays Slovakia, Bele Keler.

title: METHODOLOGICAL CHALLENGES IN TEACHING WRITING WITH CHATGPT
abstract: This study addresses the methodological challenges encountered in teaching writing using ChatGPT. It explores the complexities of designing effective instructional strategies, collecting relevant data, and interpreting results in the context of integrating AI technology into the writing classroom. The research sheds light on the multifaceted nature of these challenges and includes issues such as incorporating AI-generated feedback, ensuring pedagogical alignment, and addressing ethical considerations. By exploring these complexities, this study offers insight into improving writing instruction with AI technology.

title: PHILOSOPHICAL AND SOCIO-EDUCATIONAL FOUNDATIONS OF SECOND CHANCE ADULT EDUCATION
abstract: In order to make the implementation of second chance education feasible, it is crucial to understand its socio-educational and philosophical foundations. This study focuses on the analysis of the key pillars that form the basis of alternative school education. Recognition of its philosophical perspectives is the starting point for integrating second chance education into educational systems. By giving adults a new chance to learn and develop their skills and personal development, it is possible to enhance the demonstration of their humanity, regardless of social background or previous experience. The submitted article aims to understand second chance education's transformative potential in relevant contexts. The object of this study is to provide a theoretical overview of the current state of empirical research on philosophical and socio-educational perspectives of second chance education.

title: ASSESSING UNDERSTANDING OF THE CONCEPT OF FUNCTION, ITS DIFFERENT REPRESENTATIONS AND THE LINKS BETWEEN THEM
abstract: In these times of change and constant development, it is important that pedagogical approaches reflect modern trends and the needs of students. In mathematics, the notion of function is one of the key concepts. Despite the fact that the concept of function starts to be built in primary school, even in secondary school many students show gaps in their understanding of the concept of function, its different representations and the links between them. Our research focuses on the application of inquiry-based teaching (IBT) in the learning of the concept and properties of functions. This paper describes the initial stage of research based on a design-based research strategy oriented towards the design and development of methodological materials for teaching functions. The second part of the paper consists of the evaluation of a test designed to assess the development of functional thinking of primary school students.

title: METHODS OF DETECTION OF CYBER BULLYING IN THE EDUCATIONAL PROCESS
abstract: Cyberbullying, as one of the many phenomena of online risky behavior, is an ever-increasing problem in the age of digitization. The paper provides a systematic overview of the methods used in the detection of selected risky behavior in the online space. Our goal is to map different quantitative and qualitative methods of cyberbullying detection. The intention is to provide an overview of available methods that are used internationally and in our conditions.
